findings.where: First screen at desktop: the handwritten red "Write to me" note in the left margin. This is the page's only real contact action (mailto).
findings.fault: The page's one action carries the least visual weight in the first screen. It is a small, tilted script note sitting alone in the empty margin, away from the headline and the lines under it. In the render it looks like an annotation on the pad, not something to click. The headline, the clipped photo and the aqueduct drawing all outweigh it, so what the eye sees first does not match what the visitor most needs to do.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff who arrive wanting to contact Mark. They scan the first screen for a way to get in touch, read the margin scribble as decoration, and either look in the nav for Contact or leave.

findings.where: "Write to me" (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com), at desktop and at phone width
findings.fault: The only way to make contact is a mailto link, and Mark's email address appears nowhere on the page. Where clicking it opens nothing, or opens the wrong mail program, the visitor has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: Bank and agency staff on locked-down work machines who use webmail. Clicking does nothing useful for them, and they have no other way to find the address.

findings.where: Article specimen: the row "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge / Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF", at both widths
findings.fault: The PDF link is bold ink in the same style as the static palette labels and table headings, and it has no underline of its own. The row's bottom rule runs under only the last line of the title, so it looks like an accidental partial underline. "PDF" is in the other column and is not part of the link, so clicking the word that names the file does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles who wants the lecture PDF. They click "PDF" and get nothing, or they don't recognise the bold title as the link at all.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel: the "Replay the note" button, at both widths
findings.fault: The button replays the "Write to me" note, which is screens away at the top of the page. Wherever a visitor presses it, nothing changes on screen, so it looks dead.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reviewing the motion sketch. They press Replay, see nothing move, and conclude the animation or the button is broken.

findings.fault: An in-page action (a button) is styled as an underlined text link, using the underline the house keeps for navigation. Nothing tells a visitor it replays something here rather than taking them somewhere.
findings.who_objects: A visitor or reviewer who expects an underlined phrase to take them to another page, and is surprised when it stays put.
